title: Tunnel & Subnet Walkthrough — collapsible tiles, inline validation, and upgrade-aware screenshots
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Create a compact, discoverable set of onboarding visuals and screenshot assets for Private/VPC customers that guides operators through tunnel setup (IPsec/SSL), subnet selection, route table basics, and upgrade-time considerations. The design should support both interactive cloud-based installs and an operator-led offline appliance flow. Deliverables: collapsible tile components for the console, annotated screenshots for docs, microcopy for inline validation/error states, motion specs for tile expansion, and an upgrade banner variant showing safe rollback points.
acceptance_criteria: Collapsible tile component exported as Figma variant with responsive states (collapsed / expanded / error / success)
Annotated screenshot set (desktop + tablet) ready for docs with captions and alt text provided
Inline validation copy covering CIDR mistakes, overlapping routes, and missing gateway IPs
Upgrade-aware UI mock showing pre-upgrade checks and rollback confirmation modal
Accessibility notes included: keyboard focus order, aria-label suggestions, contrast checks
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha: Initial concept sketches uploaded to Figma. Emphasis on progressive disclosure so novice operators see a short path while advanced users can expand tile details.

2026-03-04 - Marcus Li (Eng): Flagged engineering constraint: we can't validate gateway IP reachability in the installer without a connectivity probe. Suggested we show a simulated 'connectivity check' step and surface live probe later in Dedicated flows.

2026-03-06 - PM review (Lena Ortiz): Recommend stronger emphasis on upgrade-time safety: show existing route snapshots and explicit rollback checkpoints. Add CTA for 'Export current network snapshot' before upgrade.

2026-03-08 - Design review (Sofie): Iterated on error microcopy to avoid jargon; replaced 'CIDR overlap' with 'Subnet ranges overlap — choose a different range' and added example CIDR patterns inline.

2026-03-10 - Accessibility review (Ravi Nair): Keyboard focus order OK. Request: add aria-expanded on tiles and ensure collapse/expand is announced by screen readers. Also requested 4.5:1 contrast for tile labels.
2026-03-12 - UX Writing (Marta Ruiz): Finalized microcopy for upgrade confirmation modal and rollback rationale; added a tooltip copy for 'Preserve routes' toggle.
2026-03-13 - QA (Jamal Reed): Creating visual regression checklist. Noted that motion spec should include a 160ms easing to match platform patterns.

2026-03-14 - Aisha: Prepared screenshot variants for docs: default, error, expanded advanced options, upgrade-warning state. Requesting engineering review of the shown network validation steps (see GitHub PR link).
design_notes: Progressive disclosure: show three primary tiles by default: 'Network tunnel', 'Subnet & routes', 'Upgrade safety'. Each tile collapses to a 56px header row with key status indicators.
Inline validation strategy: validate CIDR format client-side, warn on simple overlaps locally, mark 'needs verification' for overlap that requires backend probe
Rollback UX: include a secondary confirmation step displaying a timestamped snapshot and an 'Export network snapshot' CTA
Offline/appliance variant: present same tiles but with 'Manual validation' steps and terminal command snippets in expandable code panels
Localization: microcopy written in simplified English; reserve extra space for German translations (approx +18% width)
follow_up_tasks: ENG-8821: Implement API endpoint for pre-upgrade network snapshot export
ENG-8892: Add aria attributes and screen-reader announcements for tile expand/collapse
PM-403: Validate compliance requirements for storing network snapshots in customer-managed KMS
DES-231000: Prepare a compact animated GIF for marketing highlighting the collapse/expand interaction
notes_for_engineering: Tile state machine: collapsed, loading, success, warning, error. Provide hooks for live probe results and last-checked timestamp
Prefer CSS-based motion with prefers-reduced-motion support. Motion duration: 160ms ease-out for enter, 120ms ease-in for exit
API integrations: expect preflight endpoints to return structured errors with fields: code, human_message, remediation_steps (design will map these to UI states)
Export snapshot: POST /api/v1/private/network/snapshot -> returns signed URL. Design assumes signed URL availability within 2s
